_comment: DELIVERY LABOR + CAPACITY MODEL — cost-to-serve, not sell price. Sell prices and vendor/tooling costs live in pricing.json; this file adds the labor side so a quote can show TRUE contribution margin instead of tooling-only margin. Contains ONLY aggregate figures: a blended delivery rate and observed hours per endpoint. No individual pay rate or named person appears here, deliberately.
_derivation: Derived 2026-07-28 from 2,734 Autotask time entries over 2026-02-01..2026-07-27 (5.9 months), joined to Datto RMM per-company endpoint counts and to loaded staff costs (Gusto payroll + the NY employer-tax math in the New Hire Break-Even workbook). Method: hours logged against each managed customer / that customer's Datto endpoint count, averaged within contract tier.
_deliveryCostPerHourNote: Blended loaded cost of one customer-facing delivery hour, weighted by who actually logs the hours. Excludes the fixed advisory retainer (owner-confirmed 2026-07-28: not a billable resource — management and guidance), which sits in the fixed pool instead. Including it would move this figure to ~$42.79/hr on ~4.7 logged hours/month and badly distort per-endpoint economics.
_hoursProxyNote: No customer is on Basic Care today, so it borrows Standard Care's measured figure. Replace it once a real customer lands there.
_comanagedNote: TCT Ally is set BELOW Standard Care by owner direction (2026-07-28): the customer's own IT staff handle day-to-day helpdesk, moves/adds/changes and projects, so TCT's included labor is tool-stack management plus an escalation bench, not front-line work. 0.15 is an estimate, not a measurement — no customer is on Ally yet. It sits deliberately above the 0.088 h/endpoint 'pure monitoring' floor (Standard Care's non-billable share) so the tier's margin is not overstated. Revisit with real data on the first Ally customer.

laborBillingModel._note: Which tiers recover labor as time-and-materials rather than absorbing it. Owner-confirmed 2026-07-28: on Basic and Standard Care anything a customer needs is billable at the hourly rate; Comprehensive includes the monitoring/security stack but bills remediation; Complete Care absorbs support; Ally bills day-to-day labor (pricing.json packages.comanaged.hourlyLabor). The labor COST in this model is charged against every tier regardless — it is real cost either way — so contribution on the hourly tiers is UNDERSTATED by whatever T&M revenue those hours recover. See _billableCaptureFinding before trying to model that revenue.
laborBillingModel._billableCaptureFinding: T&M revenue is deliberately NOT modelled, because the source data cannot support it. Over the 6-month window the share of customer hours flagged billable was 65.4% on Standard, 63.4% on Comprehensive and 69.1% on Complete — i.e. Complete Care, which is supposed to be all-inclusive, shows the SAME billable share as the tiers that bill hourly. The flag therefore does not track each tier's commercial model, so it cannot be used to derive recovered revenue. Verifying actual capture needs the invoiced status from BillingItems (autotask_search_time_entries with withBillingStatus=true), which was not reachable when this was derived.

capacity._note: Scalable capacity counts the two offshore delivery contractors only (one full-time at 160 h/mo, one part-time at 86.7 h/mo, both net of PTO and holidays). The owner's own delivery hours are real but not scalable capacity, and the advisory retainer carries no hours. A third contractor present in the historical data left before this model was derived and is excluded.

_monthlyFixedPoolNote: Everything that does NOT scale with an added endpoint: both offshore delivery contractors, the owner's loaded cost, the advisory retainer, the non-technical admin seat, and shop overhead tooling (Kaseya 365 Ops, MSP Success Pro, Thread base). Used only for the break-even endpoint count, never charged into a quote.
_flags: Endpoint counts come from Datto RMM and include servers plus any stale or non-billable devices; the billing team's own stale-device log shows drift, which would move hours-per-endpoint.
Offshore loaded costs come from the break-even workbook, which uses $177.23/seat tooling where the app uses $218.73 — each offshore figure is understated by roughly $40/month.
48% of all logged time in the source window was internal rather than customer-facing. That is the growth runway and also the main risk: internal work rarely shrinks on its own.
Hours per endpoint is an average across a small population (7-9 companies per tier). Use it for pricing decisions, not for predicting a single customer.
